quote: "Four nights, one vehicle, your own tracker. That's how you get the frame. [Draft — J.W. to approve]" — J. W.
answer: Leopards Through the Lens is a 5-day photographic safari at Londolozi from James Wild & Co.: four nights at Varty Camp with a private vehicle and your own ranger and tracker, Lightroom tuition and print preparation at the Photographic Studio, and Canon and Nikon rentals. You go by road from Johannesburg, with an optional two nights at Ellerman House in Cape Town to finish.

days.title: Johannesburg to Varty Camp
days.line: By road to Londolozi · time on request
days.body: By road from Johannesburg (OR Tambo): the N12 and N4 east to Nelspruit, the R40 through White River to Hazyview, then the R536 towards Paul Kruger Gate. About 37 km along it, a gravel road turns off to the Sabi Sand's Shaws Gate, where the reserve charges an entry fee per person and per vehicle. From the gate it is about 17 km to camp, following Londolozi's signs.
days.acts: Arrival · meet your ranger and tracker

days.title: Your own vehicle
days.line: Private vehicle, your own ranger and tracker
days.body: A private vehicle for the whole stay, with your own ranger and tracker, so the time at each sighting is yours. Londolozi reports 75 to 100 leopard sightings a month, and guests usually see two or three leopards in three nights.
days.move: Private game drive [times to confirm with the lodge]
days.img: PHOTO · LEOPARD CUBS IN A TREE

days.title: The Photographic Studio
days.body: Time at Varty Camp's Photographic Studio between drives: Lightroom tuition on your own frames, and help preparing prints. Canon and Nikon rentals are available [kit to confirm].
days.move: On foot, then private game drive

days.title: The last light on the Sand River
days.body: Londolozi sits on the Sand River in the western Sabi Sand, unfenced to Kruger National Park. A last full day on the private vehicle, and a session at the Studio to prepare the prints you take home.
days.move: Private game drive [times to confirm with the lodge]

days.title: Home, or on to the Cape
days.line: By road to Johannesburg, or by air to Cape Town
days.body: By road back to Johannesburg (time on request). Or, to finish slowly, fly to Cape Town for two nights at Ellerman House, about 26 km, around 30 minutes, from the airport. Londolozi has its own airstrip, used by charter flights.
days.img: PHOTO · ELLERMAN HOUSE FROM THE AIR

faqs: What is included in Leopards Through the Lens?
Four nights at Londolozi Varty Camp, a private vehicle with your own ranger and tracker, and Lightroom tuition and print preparation at the Photographic Studio. Canon and Nikon rentals are available.
Can I rent camera equipment at Londolozi?
Yes. Canon and Nikon rentals are available at Londolozi; we confirm the kit for your dates.
How many leopards will I see?
Londolozi reports 75 to 100 leopard sightings a month, and guests usually see two or three leopards in three nights. This route gives you four.
Varty Camp welcomes children aged six and over.
Yes. The route can finish with two nights at Ellerman House in Cape Town, by air from Londolozi.
It is a low-risk malaria area. Precautions are still advised; ask your doctor before you travel.
How much does Leopards Through the Lens cost?
It is quoted against your dates and travellers, with any current offer applied. James Wild & Co does not publish a fixed price for this route.
